deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 13% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 10.1% = 10-year Treasury 5.1% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 83% last year; 110%/yr over 3 years — the market expects a slowdown from its recent pace.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 81% (3 years ago 47%, rising) — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $81 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 84% (3 years ago 38%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Signed but not yet delivered (remaining performance obligations): $3.2B, up 68% from a year ago — about 1% of the last 12 months of sales; customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $6.4B, up 215% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Earnings-quality red flags
flags: Receivables (money customers still owe) up 127% vs quarterly sales up 106% (days to collect 54 → 60). Customers may be paying more slowly, or sales were pulled forward.

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 110%/yr over 3 years and 69%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 65% vs a 5-year range of 16–65% (median 56%): near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back).

note.headline: NVIDIA falls 4.12% to 156.14 before tomorrow's report; hold, no trade

summary.thesis: NVIDIA is a grade A business, and at 156.14 its price assumes slower cash-flow growth than its recent results show, but the stock is falling, has no support level below it, and reports earnings tomorrow.
summary.decision: Long-term: hold. Swing: no trade until after the 2026-11-17 report.
summary.act_at: Hold at 156.14; add near 151.37 only after a clean report; trim near 224.74

note.happening: NVDA fell 4.12% to 156.14. It is in a downtrend, below its 20-day (195.64), 50-day (213.15) and 200-day (203.75) averages, and no support zone sits below the price. NVIDIA reports earnings on 2026-11-17. On 2026-11-16 the company announced the Rubin HPC GPU and the expanded Vera CPU platform, and said it swept the MLPerf benchmarks. A TechCrunch headline reported Sam Altman discussing 'Nvidia without Jensen Huang', which keeps the reported leadership questions in the news.
note.business: Things that change the business: in the latest reported quarter, sales grew 105.85% from a year earlier, up from 73.21% two quarters before. Operating margin rose to 65.21% from 58.09%. Free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) was 127.0B over the last year, up from 72.0B. Cash and liquidity are not a worry: net cash is 23.2B. Two things in the filings are at risk. First, margin is at the top of its 5-year range of 16–65%. Second, unpaid customer bills grew 127% while quarterly sales grew 106%, so some sales may have been pulled forward or customers may be paying more slowly. Things that change sentiment or governance: today's product news (Rubin HPC, Vera, quantum work) comes from company announcements, not filings, and gives no revenue figures, so it supports the long-term story without changing near-term numbers. The reported CEO questions and $946.6M of insider sales outside pre-set plans are governance and sentiment issues. They do not show up in demand or cash today. Segment data is not available, so data alone cannot tell us which product lines drive growth.

worth.text: At 156.14, the market is pricing free cash flow to start growing about 20.8% a year and then slow down. A discounted cash-flow model (today's value of future cash, at a 10.1% discount rate) gives 151.37 at 20% starting growth and 220.46 at 30%. The model's base case is 224.74, with a bear case of 193.13 and a bull case of 267.17. Valued on its own past price-to-sales levels, the stock comes out at 217.35–411.04, because the current price-to-sales of 12.4 sits at only the 9.0th percentile of its own 5-year range. It is also below the peer median of 16.6. The earnings multiple is 19.7 on trailing results and 9.9 on next year's estimates. The gap between methods comes down to one assumption: growth. Analysts expect 70% EPS growth next year, but the model caps starting growth at 30%. Margin is the other big lever. If operating margin falls to 48%, value drops to 113.77. At 32%, it drops to 76.17. My range is 151.37–224.74.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow starts growing 20–30% a year and operating margin stays near today's 65.21% instead of fading toward 48%.
